result:
Inline and shared metrics on the same experiment should now always end up with distinct identifiers, in both scenarios. I haven't run any tests and didn't add one, and I haven't checked whether any existing test relied on a created shared metric keeping the identifier it was sent with.

- **Promotion:** `create_saved_metric` in `experiment_saved_metric_service.py` now always gives a new shared metric a fresh identifier. It ignores any identifier in the incoming query, so a promoted metric no longer collides with the inline copy left on the experiment. Updates still keep the shared metric's own identifier.
- **Update with only shared metrics:** `update_experiment` in `experiment_service.py` now checks the stored inline metrics against the newly attached shared metrics. If there's a clash, it regenerates the inline metric's identifier and appends it to the ordering.
- **Agent guidance:** In `metric-configuration.md.j2`, I removed the "create with the same query, then attach" advice. It now says to create a shared metric, attach it, and remove the inline duplicate, so the experiment doesn't show the same metric twice.

I only looked at the backend and the guidance. I didn't check whether the frontend promote flow sends its own identifier, which the new backend behavior would override.
